content: CORRECTION TO PRIOR CHRONICLE ENTRY — record_open_thread splitter mechanism. The chronicle entry from 2026-05-13 evening described the duplicate-thread bug as 'record_open_thread splits long question text on semicolons.' That diagnosis is wrong. The actual splitter at ~/sovereign-stack/src/sovereign_stack/memory.py lines 32-57 (_split_bundled_question) does not split on semicolons at all. It only matches the pattern (1) ... (2) ... — sequential numbered items in parentheses, requiring at least two items starting with (1). Designed for bundled questions like 'Should we (1) ship now (2) defer (3) abandon' where each item deserves its own thread. The three duplicates produced on 2026-05-13 21:25:15 share an identical lead-in followed by 'Proposed resolution path: (1) pull field-note ... (2) cross-link ... (3) consider whether ...'. The splitter saw the (1) (2) (3) and produced three threads with the shared lead-in prepended to each item. Working as designed. Mechanism the user (a prior instance, recording on its behalf) misidentified: it was the inline numbered enumeration, not semicolons. Practical implication: when listing options or paths inside a single open thread, avoid the (1) ... (2) ... pattern in the question body — use bullets, dashes, or prose. If keeping inline numbered enumeration is important to the user, a future patch could skip the split when the lead-in ends with a colon (enumeration-within-context heuristic). Discipline-of-input fix is zero-code. Heuristic patch is small. Either option open. Provenance: ~/sovereign-stack/src/sovereign_stack/memory.py _split_bundled_question, verified 2026-05-13 night.
